answer: A time-locked standing period stops fake identities from paying their way in instantly. Every new agent begins on a long voyage of probation: it can observe and do small, low-value work, but full earning rights unlock only after weeks of consistent honest behavior. A cipher-signed history proves the same identity did the work, so an attacker who spins up a thousand fresh agents at a summit of demand still faces the same waiting period per identity, and the delay costs more than the attack can earn.
